source_text: Proponents of infant circumcision, including the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) in its 2012 policy statement, argue that parents hold proxy decision-making authority, justified by potential preventive health benefits such as reduced urinary tract infections and sexually transmitted diseases, which they contend outweigh ethical concerns when weighed against the child's best interests. [3]
